title: Uniqueness of the APIs in Seebra's Explore catalog
summary: Each API has a description and categories; TF-IDF vectors of the descriptions give similarities and nearest neighbours; the categories give crowding. Uniqueness combines both.

concepts.label: API
concepts.description: An item of kind api in the Explore catalog.

children.label: Description
children.description: Title, tags, summary and description text: what is measured, not the API's data.

children.label: Distinctness
children.description: 1 − mean cosine similarity to the k nearest descriptions.

children.label: Rarity
children.description: 1 − n/(2(n+20)), n the other APIs in its least crowded category.

concepts.label: TF-IDF similarity
concepts.description: Cosine of TF-IDF word vectors: (1 + log tf) · log((1 + N)/(1 + df)), normalised.

children.label: Nearest neighbours
children.description: The k APIs with the most similar descriptions.

children.label: Place names
children.description: Country and city words removed, so per-country copies look alike.

concepts.label: Field
concepts.description: The catalog's category tree (top-level field / category), e.g. science/chemistry.

facts.text: Science and engineering categories follow the OECD Fields of Science and Technology (Frascati Manual).

concepts.label: Near-copy
concepts.description: Two APIs whose descriptions share most weighted words (cosine > 0.5): vendor product lines, per-country twins.

children.label: Vendor family
children.description: One provider's products described from one template.

children.label: Per-country copy
children.description: The same kind of service for another country (grid operators, statistics offices).

concepts.label: Catalog snapshot
concepts.description: The catalog's updated time: scores change as APIs are added.
